find: - **Shards.** The alone block's folders run side by side, each in a shard: a fixed-path workspace, `~/deepbuild-shards/<k>/`, holding the worktree's exact tree written in place by the bays' rule (section 4), its own `target/` kept across runs, and the worktree's `node_modules/` and package builds cloned copy-on-write each use (macOS's `cp -c`; elsewhere GNU `cp --reflink=auto`, which copies where the disk can't clone, as on ext4). On macOS a new shard starts from a clone of the worktree's files, `target/` with them; elsewhere git writes its tree alone and it builds its own `target/`, since a copy would be many GB a shard. On macOS too, a folder that is or holds another worktree of the repository, as the main checkout's `.claude/worktrees/` does, stays behind. A folder still runs one file at a time, and only in one shard at once, so its files and its builds never meet another's: a sibling's cargo build rewrites `target/debug/<bin>` only in the shard it runs in. The shards run beside the parallel block, on the run's one test grant (section 6), and `DEEP_SHARDS` sets how many, half the cores by default. A shard is taken, new or reused, only while the disk holds 5 GB for it above #1017's 30 GB floor, since its tests' builds grow it; with none, the block runs in the worktree as before. A new shard's first builds compile the workspace crates its tests build at its own path: deep-hook and deep-show took 2.4 minutes and 3.4 GB, the whole workspace about 3.5 minutes and 6 GB. A shard leaves when a run that claims shards finds that no live process holds it and that it was last made a tree more than three days before: the run takes the shard's lock, removes the shard and then the lock, highest number first, and prints one line, the shards removed and the bytes `du` gave for them (#3547). When it was last made a tree is the time of its `.git/packed-refs`, which each use writes, and three days is hygiene's figure for an idle `target/` (section 9).
